backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same radius-2, 2048-bit generator so each feature is the number of times a substructure occurs. Keep the RandomForestRegressor unchanged. Counts carry more information than presence bits for size-dependent properties like permeability.
backlog.title: Morgan count fingerprints instead of bits

backlog.spec: Build the generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()) so atoms are grouped by pharmacophore class (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than element identity. Keep the random forest and everything else fixed. This gives more generalizable features across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP-style) fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the full RDKit Descriptors.descList values for each molecule (replacing NaN/inf with 0 and clipping extreme values) and concatenate them to the Morgan bit vector before fitting the random forest. Physicochemical descriptors such as TPSA, logP, and H-bond counts are strongly tied to passive permeability, so the forest gets a direct signal it lacks from bits alone.
backlog.title: Append RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Drop the fingerprint entirely and featurize each molecule with only the RDKit Descriptors.descList values (NaN and inf set to 0, columns with zero variance removed). Fit the same random forest on that matrix. Tests whether a compact set of physically meaningful properties generalizes better across unseen scaffolds than hashed substructure bits.
backlog.title: Descriptor-only random forest

backlog.spec: Concatenate the 167 MACCS structural keys (rdMolDescriptors.GetMACCSKeysFingerprint, converted to a numpy array) to the Morgan features before the random forest. MACCS keys are a curated set of functional groups that encode polarity and ring information in a compact, interpretable form.
backlog.title: MACCS keys added to fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan features with the concatenation of hashed atom-pair count fingerprints and topological-torsion count fingerprints (each 1024 bits, from rdFingerprintGenerator's atom-pair and torsion generators). Keep the random forest. These encode long-range topology and shape-related information that circular fingerprints miss.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute a short hand-picked vector per molecule: molecular weight, Crippen logP, TPSA, number of H-bond donors and acceptors, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, formal charge, heavy atom count, and counts of carboxylic acid and basic amine SMARTS matches. Concatenate this vector to the Morgan bits. Acids and bases and polarity drive ionization-dependent Caco-2 permeability, so these features target the known mechanistic drivers.
backlog.title: Physicochemical rule-of-thumb features

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with a LightGBM regressor (objective regression, around 600 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.5, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, random_state=seed). Use the same features as the baseline, Morgan bits plus RDKit descriptors. Gradient boosting often beats bagged trees on small tabular data.
backlog.title: LightGBM regressor on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Train a LightGBM regressor with objective='l1' (median regression) on Morgan plus descriptor features. The evaluation metric is mean absolute error, so fitting the conditional median rather than the mean should reduce the loss directly. Use about 800 trees with learning_rate 0.03 and seed-controlled bagging.
backlog.title: LightGBM with absolute-error objective

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with objective='reg:absoluteerror', max_depth 6, learning_rate 0.03, n_estimators 700, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, and random_state=seed. Train on Morgan bits plus RDKit descriptors. Provides a second strong gradient boosting learner whose median objective matches the MAE metric.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error loss

backlog.spec: Fit CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE', depth 6, iterations 1000, learning_rate 0.05, verbose=0, random_seed=seed, on the RDKit descriptor matrix concatenated with Morgan counts. CatBoost's ordered boosting is comparatively resistant to overfitting on small datasets, which suits 728 molecules.
backlog.title: CatBoost with MAE loss on descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard on bits) similarity matrix between training and test molecules from the Morgan bit vectors, and fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed', C around 5, epsilon 0.1. Predict using the test-to-train kernel. Chemically meaningful similarity kernels are well known to work strongly on small molecular datasets.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Use the Tanimoto similarity matrix on Morgan count or bit fingerprints as a precomputed kernel, and solve kernel ridge regression with a regularization strength alpha near 0.5 by adding alpha*I to the training Gram matrix and solving via numpy.linalg.solve after centering the target on its training mean. Return the test-to-train kernel times the dual coefficients plus the mean. Gives a smooth similarity-based predictor distinct from tree models.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, compute Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules using Morgan bit vectors, take the k=7 most similar training molecules, and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their targets (weights = similarity to the power 3). Pure nearest-neighbour averaging is a cheap, interpretable baseline that complements forests.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted k-nearest neighbors

backlog.spec: Build the RDKit descriptor matrix, replace NaN/inf with 0, clip to the 1st and 99th percentiles per column, standardize with training-set statistics, and fit sklearn Ridge with alpha around 10. Linear models on physicochemical descriptors are known to capture much of the Caco-2 trend and are a smooth, low-variance counterpart to trees.
backlog.title: Ridge regression on standardized descriptors

backlog.spec: Train sklearn MLPRegressor on Morgan bit vectors (hidden layers (256, 64), alpha=1e-3 L2 weight decay, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.1, max_iter 500, random_state=seed). Average predictions from 5 MLPs trained with seeds derived from the given seed. Neural nets trained with weight decay and seed averaging give a different inductive bias from forests.
backlog.title: Multi-layer perceptron ensemble on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Change the random forest criterion to 'absolute_error' so each split minimizes the MAE-related impurity rather than squared error. Limit the cost by setting max_samples=0.7 with bootstrap enabled. Keep the other settings. Matching the split criterion to the reported metric can reduce error on skewed targets.
backlog.title: Random forest with absolute-error splitting

backlog.spec: Fit the baseline random forest on Morgan bits and a LightGBM regressor (l1 objective, around 600 trees) on Morgan plus descriptor features, then return the simple average of the two predictions. Averaging two different learners typically reduces variance more than tuning either one alone.
backlog.title: Blend random forest with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold KFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from three base learners: random forest on Morgan bits, LightGBM on Morgan plus descriptors, and SVR with Tanimoto kernel. Fit a non-negative linear regression meta-model on the stacked out-of-fold predictions, then refit the base learners on all training data and apply the meta-model to the test predictions.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: Train the random forest three times with different random_state values derived from the given seed, each with 300 trees, and average the three prediction vectors. This reduces the Monte Carlo variance of the forest predictions, which is a small but measurable component of the fold-level noise.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged random forest bagging

backlog.spec: Use a LightGBM regressor with bagging_fraction 0.5, bagging_freq 1, feature_fraction 0.3, and min_child_samples 10, trained on Morgan bits plus descriptors. Strong subsampling at each boosting round regularizes the model against memorizing specific training scaffolds, which matters because test folds contain unseen ring skeletons.
backlog.title: Subsampled stochastic gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Keep the random forest on Morgan bits but raise min_samples_leaf to 3 and lower max_features to 0.1, and increase the number of trees to 500. Fewer features per split and larger leaves smooth the predictions for molecules that lie far from the training distribution, which is the situation in scaffold-held-out folds.
backlog.title: Stronger random forest regularization

backlog.spec: For LightGBM on Morgan plus descriptor features, carve out a random 10 percent of the training molecules with the seed as the split seed, train with early_stopping(50) on that validation portion using the l1 objective and a maximum of 2000 rounds, then refit on all training data using the best iteration count found. Automatic round selection avoids hand-tuned tree counts that are wrong for each fold.
backlog.title: Early stopping for boosted trees via internal split

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM on Morgan plus descriptor features with learning_rate 0.01 and 2000 rounds using the l1 objective, feature_fraction 0.5, and bagging_fraction 0.8. A smaller shrinkage with more rounds usually gives a smoother fit and slightly better generalization than a coarse learning rate, at modest extra cost on 728 molecules.
backlog.title: Lower learning rate with more boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles, computed on the training fold only, then fit the random forest on Morgan bits as usual. The Caco-2 measurements contain a few extreme values that pull fitted leaves toward outliers, and clipping reduces this influence on the test predictions.
backlog.title: Winsorize extreme training targets

backlog.spec: Keep the random forest fit unchanged, but instead of returning the mean of the tree predictions, compute the per-molecule median across all trees by stacking model.estimators_ predictions. The median of tree outputs is more robust to a few trees that extrapolate badly on unseen scaffolds, which aligns with the MAE objective.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees prediction from the forest

backlog.spec: Before fitting, drop training molecules whose canonical SMILES appear more than once and average their target values, so each unique structure contributes once. Also keep only one representative of molecules with identical Morgan bit vectors. Duplicates over-weight certain chemotypes in the forest and can bias the fitted model toward them.
backlog.title: Remove duplicate and near-duplicate training molecules

backlog.spec: Compute each training molecule's mean Tanimoto similarity to the other training molecules, and set its sample weight to the inverse of that density (normalized to mean 1). Pass the weights to the random forest or LightGBM fit. Molecules from densely populated chemotypes then count less, so the model spends capacity on under-represented regions likely to appear in unseen-scaffold test folds.
backlog.title: Inverse-density sample weighting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 3 Murcko-scaffold-grouped folds using GroupKFold on scaffold SMILES, and choose the best of three random forest settings (max_features in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} with min_samples_leaf in {1, 3}) by mean absolute error on the inner held-out folds. Refit the best setting on all training data. Selecting hyperparameters on scaffold-held-out data mirrors the evaluation protocol and avoids leaking test skeletons into tuning.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter selection by inner scaffold CV

backlog.spec: Keep the current XGBRegressor setup. Pass monotone_constraints as a tuple with one entry per feature column: +1 for MolLogP (permeability rises with lipophilicity), -1 for TPSA, NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors, and -1 for MolWt; 0 for every Morgan bit. Build the tuple from the column count of featurize() so it matches exactly. No other changes.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on physchem descriptors in XGBoost

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, standardize the 5 descriptor columns (fit the scaler on train only) and fit a RidgeRegression (alpha around 1.0) on them to predict train_y. Compute out-of-fold ridge predictions on the training set with a 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) so the residuals are not optimistic. Fit the existing XGBRegressor on the fingerprint+descriptor features to the residuals (train_y minus OOF ridge prediction). At prediction time, add the ridge prediction from a model fit on all training data to the XGB residual prediction.
backlog.title: Ridge base model with XGBoost on residuals

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule. Draw B=8 bootstrap samples by sampling scaffold groups with replacement (keeping all molecules of a sampled scaffold together), using a numpy RNG seeded from the seed argument. Fit one XGBRegressor (same hyperparameters, random_state set per bag) on each sample and average the test predictions. This targets the scaffold shift the harness uses, and it is a single function change with no new packages.
backlog.title: Scaffold-group bootstrap bagging of XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace objective='reg:absoluteerror' with objective='reg:pseudohubererror' and set huber_slope=0.5 (try 1.0 as a second setting if time permits). Keep all other XGBoost settings. The pseudo-Huber loss is smooth near zero, so gradients and leaf values are better behaved than with the pure L1 loss, and it still down-weights large outliers the way MAE does. Keep the predictions unmodified.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber objective instead of absolute error

backlog.spec: Change the XGBRegressor to booster='dart' with rate_drop=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and one_drop=True, keeping n_estimators, learning_rate, depth, subsample and colsample_bytree as they are (set n_estimators to about 500 because dart is slower to converge). DART randomly drops previously built trees during boosting, which regularizes the ensemble against a few dominant splits. Keep objective='reg:absoluteerror' and random_state=seed.
backlog.title: DART booster with dropout on trees

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute the column-wise count of nonzero Morgan bits over the training molecules only. Drop every fingerprint column whose support is below 3 molecules, and apply the same column mask to the test features. Keep all descriptor columns. This removes bits that are seen in one or two molecules and mostly act as noise for the scaffold-held-out split. Use a fixed threshold, not a tuned one.
backlog.title: Prune rare fingerprint bits by training support

backlog.spec: Build three feature sets from the same atom-invariant Morgan generator with radius 1, 2 and 3 (2048 bits each, plus the 5 descriptors). Fit one XGBRegressor (current hyperparameters, random_state=seed) per feature set and average the three test predictions with equal weights. Radius 1 captures local chemistry, radius 3 captures larger environments, and averaging three differently-biased models should reduce variance without any tuning.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Morgan ensemble

backlog.spec: Fit the existing XGBRegressor on train features, then compute its in-sample predictions. Form residuals r = train_y minus those predictions, using out-of-fold predictions from a 5-fold split to avoid optimism. For each test molecule, find its k=5 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on the Morgan bit vectors (computed with numpy: intersection over union on dense 0/1 arrays), and add a similarity-weighted mean of their residuals, weighted by sim**3 and scaled by 0.5. This is a local correction layer that only activates when a close analog exists in the training set.
backlog.title: Tanimoto nearest-neighbor correction of XGBoost residuals

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit the current XGBRegressor on the training set and predict test_smiles. Then take the 25 percent of test molecules whose nearest training neighbor has Tanimoto similarity above 0.6 (compute from Morgan bits) as the confident set. Append those test molecules with their predicted values to the training data and refit the model once. Return the refit predictions for the full test set. No labels from the held-out test are used, only the model's own predictions on the molecules passed in, so this is legal transductive learning.
backlog.title: Self-training with confident test-set pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: For each molecule, embed one conformer with rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule (random seed from the seed argument, maxAttempts 50), optimize with MMFFOptimizeMolecule, then compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcPMI1, CalcPMI2, CalcPMI3, CalcRadiusOfGyration, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2, and CalcAsphericity. Append these 8 values to the feature matrix. If embedding fails for a molecule, fall back to the 2D-only features with zeros for these columns. Permeability depends on molecular shape and size, which fingerprints capture only indirectly.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from ETKDG conformers

backlog.spec: Replace the 5 hand-picked descriptors with the full Descriptors.descList set, computed for every molecule. Replace NaN and infinite values with 0 and clip each column to its 1st-99th percentile computed on the training fold. Use these columns for the Ridge base (after StandardScaler) and append them to the Morgan bits as input to the XGBRegressor. Drop constant columns before fitting. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Wrap each descriptor call in try/except so one failing molecule returns zeros.
backlog.title: Full RDKit 2D descriptor set in the residual model

backlog.spec: Add a small block of integer count features from RDKit SMARTS patterns for ionization and polarity: carboxylic acid, aliphatic primary/secondary/tertiary amine, quaternary nitrogen, phenol, sulfonic or phosphate acid, and amide. Compute each with Chem.MolFromSmarts and len(mol.GetSubstructMatches). Append these 7 to X_all so the XGBRegressor sees them. Leave the Ridge base on its current 5 descriptors. This tests whether charge state, which governs Caco-2 transport, is missing from the feature set.
backlog.title: Ionization-class SMARTS counts

backlog.spec: Add a learned per-bit prior. For each of the 2048 Morgan bits, compute the mean training residual over molecules where the bit is set, shrunk toward the global mean with a smoothing constant of 10 (weight = n / (n + 10)). Compute these encodings out-of-fold inside the training set with a 5-fold split to avoid leakage. For each molecule, take the mean of its bits' encodings as one extra feature, and append it to X_all. For test molecules, use encodings fitted on the full training set. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Smoothed out-of-fold target encoding of fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Replace the linear Ridge base on 5 descriptors with an additive model. Apply sklearn SplineTransformer (degree 3, n_knots 5, extrapolation 'linear') to the 5 standardized descriptors, then fit Ridge(alpha=1.0) on the spline features. Keep the out-of-fold residual step and the XGBRegressor unchanged, using the same OOF procedure with this new base. The change is a GAM-like nonlinear base in place of a linear one.
backlog.title: Spline-based additive base model instead of Ridge

backlog.spec: Replace the squared-error Ridge base with a median-regression base. Fit sklearn QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=0.01, solver='highs') on the standardized 5 descriptors, in both the OOF loop and the final fit. The base then minimizes absolute error, matching the MAE metric and the XGBoost objective. Keep the XGBoost residual step as is. This tests whether a robust base reduces outlier pull on the residuals.
backlog.title: MAE-fitted linear base model

backlog.spec: Before fitting the XGBRegressor on residuals, augment the training set with 1000 synthetic rows. Each row mixes two random training rows i and j: x = lam*x_i + (1-lam)*x_j and target = lam*r_i + (1-lam)*r_j, with lam drawn from Beta(0.4, 0.4) using a seed-derived RandomState. Pair indices with a permutation. Concatenate the synthetic rows to the real ones and fit as before. Only the training rows are mixed, never the test rows.
backlog.title: Feature-space mixup augmentation for the residual booster

backlog.spec: Keep the XGBRegressor and its settings, but use xgboost's callback API to schedule the learning rate. Pass a LearningRateScheduler-style callback (xgboost.callback.TrainingCallback subclass, or a simple per-round function that calls booster.set_param) that decays the learning rate from 0.06 at round 0 to 0.006 at the final round along a cosine curve. Keep N_ESTIMATORS at 700 and the same subsampling. Use seed for all randomness. This is a schedule change in place of the constant LEARNING_RATE.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay for XGBoost

backlog.spec: After computing the full-training blended prediction, fit a 2-parameter calibration y = a*pred + b. Get the training-set predictions out of fold: for each of 5 inner folds (KFold on the train set, seeded), fit the Ridge and XGB pieces on 4 folds and predict the held-out fold. Fit a and b by minimizing MAE on these OOF predictions (scipy.optimize.minimize with Nelder-Mead, starting from a=1, b=0). Apply a and b to the final test predictions. This corrects shrinkage or stretch that the boosted residual model introduces.
backlog.title: Post-hoc linear calibration of the blended prediction

backlog.spec: Split the training set by molecular weight at its median, computed from the training fold only. Fit one complete pipeline (the current Ridge plus XGBRegressor residual model) on the small-molecule half and another on the large-molecule half. At prediction time, route each test molecule to the expert for its MW side. Use a minimum of 100 training molecules per expert, and fall back to the single full-data pipeline if a side has fewer. This tests whether permeability drivers differ by size regime.
backlog.title: Molecular-weight gated two-expert model

backlog.spec: Train 5 copies of the residual XGBRegressor, each with random_state = seed + k for k in 0..4, and colsample_bytree=0.3 instead of 0.5 so the copies see different feature subsets. Average their residual predictions on the test set, then add the Ridge prediction as before. Reuse one OOF residual vector for all copies. Keep N_ESTIMATORS at 700 per copy so total fit time stays under the 10-minute job limit. Use seed for all randomness.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged XGBoost residual ensemble with column-subsampling

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, map y_all to a normal distribution with sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(len(y),200), random_state=seed) fitted on the training targets only. Run the existing Ridge-then-XGBoost residual pipeline on the transformed target. Ridge and XGBoost residuals are then computed in the transformed space. Before returning, apply the fitted transformer's inverse_transform to the summed prediction (ridge_pred + xgb_res_pred). Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-Gauss transform of the target

backlog.spec: Replace the bit fingerprint with Morgan count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, radius 2, feature invariants kept). Compute inverse document frequency weights from the training fold only: idf_j = log((1+n)/(1+df_j))+1, where df_j is the number of training molecules with a nonzero count in column j. Multiply the count matrix by idf and L2-normalise each row. Keep the 5 RDKit descriptors appended as before and drop any column with zero training variance. Use the same XGBoost residual model on the weighted matrix.
backlog.title: IDF-weighted Morgan count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge base model on 5 descriptors with an ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, l1_ratio=0.5, max_iter=5000) fitted on the standardised full feature matrix (fingerprint bits plus descriptors). Keep the existing out-of-fold residual scheme for the XGBoost stage, with the 5-fold split seeded by seed. The XGBoost model then fits the OOF residuals of this linear base on the full feature matrix. The prediction is the elastic-net prediction plus the XGBoost residual prediction.
backlog.title: Elastic-net linear base model on full fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge base model with KernelRidge(kernel='laplacian', alpha=1.0, gamma=1/n_features) fitted on the standardised 5 RDKit descriptors. Fit it with the same OOF residual procedure. The XGBoost residual model stays as it is. Scale descriptors with StandardScaler fitted on training folds only. Keep the random seed for any tie-breaking.
backlog.title: Laplacian kernel ridge on standardised descriptors as base

backlog.spec: Cluster the training fingerprint bit matrix with KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=seed, n_init=5). Fit one independent XGBoost residual model per cluster, with the same hyperparameters but fewer rounds (about 300) to limit overfitting. At prediction time, assign each test molecule to its nearest training centroid with kmeans.predict and use that cluster's model. Fall back to a single global XGBoost model for any cluster with fewer than 30 training molecules.
backlog.title: k-means mixture-of-experts gating

backlog.spec: Build a fixed random graph encoder in numpy. For each molecule, use atom features (one-hot element, degree, aromaticity, H-count, in-ring flag), and project them with a fixed random matrix W0 drawn from np.random.default_rng(seed). Run 3 rounds of message passing: h <- tanh(A_norm @ h @ W_k), with A_norm the row-normalised adjacency including self-loops and random W_k. Concatenate the sum-pooled and max-pooled vectors from each round as features, standardise, and append them to the existing Morgan bits and descriptors. Feed the combined matrix to the existing XGBoost residual model. The encoder is never trained.
backlog.title: Random-weight graph convolution features (untrained message passing)

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after computing the OOF residuals of the base model, identify the 10% of training molecules with the largest absolute OOF residual. Drop them from the training set for the XGBoost residual stage only. Refit XGBoost on the remaining 90% using the existing OOF residual targets. The base ridge model stays fitted on all training data. Prediction is unchanged: ridge_pred plus the trimmed XGBoost prediction.
backlog.title: Trimmed refit on high out-of-fold residuals

backlog.spec: Train the existing XGBoost residual model once with N_ESTIMATORS=700. At prediction time, call predict with iteration_range covering 3 checkpoints: (0,350), (0,525) and (0,700). Average the three resulting residual predictions and add the ridge prediction. This smooths the boosting trajectory without extra training cost. Keep all other hyperparameters the same.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging across boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan bit fingerprints for both train_smiles and test_smiles. Build the fingerprint vocabulary from bits that are nonzero in at least 2 molecules across the union of train and test molecules, so both sides share the same columns. The descriptors and the ridge stage still use training data only. Fit the XGBoost residual model on the training rows only and predict the test rows. This is an unsupervised use of test SMILES that never touches test labels.
backlog.title: Transductive fingerprint vocabulary over train and test SMILES

backlog.spec: Before the main model, define 4 auxiliary targets from RDKit descriptors computed for training molecules: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt and NumRotatableBonds. For each auxiliary target, fit a small XGBoost regressor (max_depth 4, 200 rounds) on the Morgan fingerprint bits using 5-fold OOF predictions within the training set. For test molecules, average the 5 fold models' predictions. Append these 4 OOF predictions as features to the fingerprint and descriptor matrix, and then run the existing ridge plus XGBoost residual pipeline on the augmented matrix.
backlog.title: Auxiliary-descriptor stacking via out-of-fold predictions

incumbent.description: Fix the shape mismatch error by using the OOF (Out-of-Fold) indexing correctly to assign predictions to the correct fold.

memo: Helped: fixing the Descriptors import (slot 1, 0.3966), pharmacophore-style atom invariants in Morgan (slot 5, 0.3725), and XGBoost residual boosting with the OOF indexing fix (slot 21, 0.3657/0.3578 over 2 runs, incumbent 0.3618). Did not help, all within noise or worse: count fingerprints (0.3695), multi-radius Morgan (0.3712), seed-averaged XGB (0.3662), QuantileRegressor base (0.3671), target winsorizing (0.3685), CatBoost residual (0.3721), LightGBM (0.3845), SVR/XGB swap (0.3790), rare-bit pruning (0.6002, likely a bug). Main problem: most slots crashed or failed to patch, so many ideas are untested. Next: make small edits and copy SEARCH text exactly from the current file. Check every import and API call before submitting. Retry one idea per slot: full RDKit 2D descriptors with NaN handling, an RF plus boosted blend, a Tanimoto kernel, and MACCS keys. Replicate any marginal gain before accepting it.
